Thought: To solve this problem, I need to evaluate the reactivity of each compound in a nucleophilic acyl substitution. Nucleophilic acyl substitution reactions involve the attack of a nucleophile on an electrophilic carbonyl carbon, resulting in the substitution of a leaving group. The reactivity order generally follows: acyl chlorides > anhydrides > esters > amides, due to the varying leaving group abilities and electron-withdrawing effects.

1. O=C(Cl)C1CCCCC1 is a cyclohexylcarbonyl chloride, an acyl chloride, which is highly reactive due to the good leaving ability of the chloride ion.
2. O=C(OC(C)C)CC1=CC=CC=C1 is an ester (specifically, an isopropyl benzoate), which is less reactive than acyl chlorides because the alkoxide ion is a poorer leaving group than chloride.
3. N[C@@H](C(C)C)C(N[C@H](CO)CC1=CC=CC=C1)=O is an amide, which is the least reactive in this context because the amide ion (NH2-) is a poor leaving group and the nitrogen can donate electron density into the carbonyl, stabilizing it.

The order from least reactive to most reactive is therefore: amide < ester < acyl chloride.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
